title: Introduce immutable release index and restore pruner to reduce rollback hazards
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Add an immutable release index (writes are append-only, signed) and a configurable restore pruner that removes orphaned/partial restores older than TTL; improves safety for rollback and upgrade workflows, adds operational metrics and runbook entries.
description: Context: In large private deployments we observed edge-case restore/rollback hazards when a partial restore (failed mid-way) left leftover release artifacts that could be accidentally selected by automated rollbacks or by operators during incident recovery. This PR introduces a Write-Once immutable release index (append-only, content-addressed entries with release metadata signatures) and a 'restore pruner' subsystem which safely identifies and reclaims stale/partial restore state after a configurable TTL. Motivation: reduce the manual toil and risk during multi-tenant restores and automated downgrade attempts; make upgrade/rollback selection deterministic and auditable. Design summary: 1) Immutable release index: a new compact index stored alongside installer artifacts (S3/GCS/MinIO or on-prem artifact store) containing release entries keyed by content-hash and signed with the private-installer keypair. Index writes are append-only and we add a migration that converts existing indices into an append-log with a compacted view. 2) Restore pruner: background controller (opt-in via installer values) that scans restore records in the installer DB and object store; it validates restore completion markers, tombstones truly orphaned artifacts, records reclamation events in audit logs, and surfaces metrics for reclaimed bytes and pruned restores. 3) Backward compatibility: index migration runs as a safe, idempotent job; when the new index is not present the installer will operate in legacy mode. 4) Operational controls: TTL, dry-run mode, rate limits, and an explicit reconciliation switch guarded by a Kubernetes feature-gate. Checklist: - [x] Add append-only index format and signer utility - [x] Migration job to build initial immutable index from existing releases - [x] Helm chart values and feature-gate for enablement - [x] Restore pruner controller with dry-run and metrics - [x] E2E integration tests for migration + prune dry-run - [x] Documentation and runbook entries for SRE/operators - [x] Terraform module updates to surface artifact-store configuration Migrated components and fallbacks: - Installer will continue to read legacy release manifests if the immutable index is absent, but a warning will be emitted in logs and the Console. - During migration the index builder uses a safe checkpointing approach to avoid partial index publication. Testing: Unit tests for signer and index append, controller unit tests, integration tests that run in a CI ephemeral MinIO + Postgres environment verifying prune/dry-run semantics. We added an e2e that performs: create release -> start restore -> inject failure -> run pruner (dry-run) -> run pruner (active) -> assert orphaned objects cleaned. Rollout plan: ship behind a Helm feature flag off by default for existing installs; enable by default for new installs after one release cycle. Gradual rollout with operator opt-in and a runbook step for running index-migration in a maintenance window. Notes on security: index entries are signed to avoid tampering across artifact stores; signer keys optionally derive from KMS/HSM configured in Private deployments. Limitations and next steps: we do not yet garbage-collect blobs referenced by legacy manifests until index compaction is enabled in a follow-up; we plan to add a cross-region index replication feature. Related: ENG-2104 (restore reliability), DEVOPS-92 (artifact cleanup).
commits: feat(installer): add immutable release index and signer utility
feat(pruner): restore-pruner controller with dry-run and metrics
helm(chart): add featureGate values and pruner config
terraform: expose artifact_store config to installer module
docs: runbook for index migration and prune operations
review_comments: Evan McCarthy: Please add a brief compatibility note in the console UI when legacy manifests are present; operators should see an explicit 'index-migration recommended' banner. - Author reply: added console warning and a follow-up ticket to design the banner copy.

Sofia Liu: Safety nit: the signer private key rotation procedure needs a clear operator path, how do we re-sign existing index entries? - Author reply: added a rotation section in the runbook that describes creating a new signed append with rotation metadata and an automated re-sign job (opt-in).

Arjun Patel: Can the pruner mistakenly remove restores that are long-running but valid? We should ensure a lock/heartbeat on in-progress restores. - Author reply: pruner respects a restore heartbeat column and skips any record with a recent heartbeat; added e2e covering long-running restore and verified pruner skip behavior.
merge_summary: Squash merged after 2 approvals. CI green. Migration and runbook docs included.
notes_for_release: Feature disabled by default for existing clusters; operators should consult docs/ops/index-migration-runbook.md before enabling. New deployments will have feature enabled after one release cycle.
